2. An extent of 0.0045 Hectors (1.11 cents) of land along with a commercial building in old Survey No. 89/12 and new Survey No. 89/25 of Kannur Village acquired for the purpose of upgradation of Thalassery-Valavupara State Highway.
The Acquisition Authority awarded an amount of Rs.15,73,334/- as compensation as per award No.27/2008 dated 12.3.2008.
Dissatisfied with the compensation amount, the revision petitioners sought reference, and the reference court enhanced the land to Rs.30,800/- per cent.

Since there was no deposit 2025:KER:22288 made by the respondents, the revision petitioners filed EP No.224/2019 claiming an amount of Rs.20,58,579/-
as on 09.10.2019.
The respondents deposited Rs.4,68,884/- and the same has already been withdrawn by the revision petitioners.
The Execution Court ordered the attachment, and the respondents filed EA No.74/2023 to lift the attachment.

The said application is allowed and held Padmini P vs Government Of Kerala on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68102360/

sentences.text: 3. A counter affidavit is filed by the respondents, in which the extent of land acquired is admitted.
It is also admitted that the structure was also acquired from the petitioners.
Along with the counter affidavit, a statement is also furnished.
A perusal of the statement would show that interest at the rate of 9% and 15% under the statute is granted along with the enhanced land value, which comes to Rs.7,925/- alone.
The interest on the structure as well as the solatium is not calculated in the statement.

The counsel for the petitioners relied on a judgment of the Apex Court in Sunder v. Union of India (2001 KHC 750), wherein the Apex Court considered whether the claimant is entitled to interest on the solatium as well.

entities.text: Sunder v. Union of India (2001 KHC 750)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Apex Court categorically held that under Section 28 of the Land Acquisition Act of 1894,
the claimants are entitled to interest on the aggregate amount, including solatium.

Thus, the order passed by the Execution Court stating that the Execution Petition is not maintainable is without appreciating the correct law laid down by the Apex Court in Sunder (supra)
and the statutory benefits available under Section 28 of the Land Acquisition Act.

Therefore, the impugned order passed on 03.10.2024 in EA No.74/2023 in EP No.224/2019 is set aside, and the Civil Judge (Sr.Division), Thalassery, is directed to reconsider the same in the light of the dictum laid down in Sunder (supra), and the statutory provisions in the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The respondents 2025:KER:22288 are at liberty to file a statement showing the amount due to the claimants.
Since the LAR is of the year 2014, there will be a further direction to dispose of EA No.74/2023 within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
CRP is disposed of as above.

Sd/-
